&api-questions;
The nbfx Diff API is the headless line comparison: Diff compares two texts line by line under DiffOptions and answers with a DiffResult, the Difference blocks of added, deleted and changed lines. It is the first part of the M-tier diff contract and is devel until its first consumer, the diff view, has landed and shown what it needs of it; Patch and Merge are planned for M2. It compares lines and nothing else: what a view shows beside them - a renamed file, a changed mode, line endings, a missing last line ending, a binary file - is for the view to tell from what it compares.
The comparison is the Hunt-McIlroy longest common subsequence, ported from the HuntDiff of NetBeans' diff module and kept package-private. The API is toolkit-free and knows nothing of files, version control or views: the lines come from wherever the caller has them, and what is done with the result is the caller's.
A diff view compares the content of a file at two points - the last commit, the index, the working tree - and draws the blocks that differ; a caller may leave out differences in case or in white space.
DiffTest covers additions, deletions and changes, the options alone and together, case folding, argument and result checking, and cancellation in every part of a comparison. The blocks are checked against the texts: that they lead from one to the other, and, against a plain longest-common-subsequence table, that they keep as many lines as the texts have in common - for every pair of small texts, for random ones with many repeated lines, and under the options. The API is under development until the MVP freeze, after which API signature tests (sigtest) are enabled.

Diff is stateless and its results are immutable: it may be called on any thread. A comparison takes time that grows with the texts and with how often their lines repeat, and nothing in the engine limits their size: a view runs it off its drawing thread, decides how large a text it compares, and cancels a comparison nobody waits for through the BooleanSupplier of Diff.compute, which is asked before the comparison starts and throughout every part of it.
